Let the common height of the vases be \(H\). Their total capacities can be found from the amount of water and the fraction of the vase that is filled:

- Vase I is half full: \(\displaystyle \text{capacity}_I=\frac{4}{1/2}=8\) L.
- Vase II is two-thirds full: \(\displaystyle \text{capacity}_{II}=\frac{3}{2/3}=4.5\) L.
- Vase III is full: \(\displaystyle \text{capacity}_{III}=4\) L.

Since the vases have the same height, their top-view areas are proportional to their capacities. Therefore,

\[
\text{area}_I>\text{area}_{II}>\text{area}_{III}.
\]
